title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regression Checks
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results, identify regressions on new quantized model variant, discuss prompt set adjustments and guardrails, agree next steps for targeted prompt tuning and benchmark retest.
topics: Quality regression observed on 3 prompt categories
Prompt set curation and scoring thresholds
Guardrail false positives on safety filter
Decision on continuing hosted variant vs dedicated for pilot
Next steps: updated eval spreadsheet, targeted reruns, meet infra for VPC config
action_items: Maya Ortiz: run per-prompt confusion matrix and share CSV (due 2025-03-14)
Jamal Reed: provide sample logs for failing queries and exact request payloads (due 2025-03-13)
Ethan Cole: send updated pricing/commit options for dedicated capacity (due 2025-03-18)
Sara Patel: mark priority prompt sets (A/B/C) and return by 2025-03-12
next_steps: Redwood to re-run evals on quantized variant with updated decoding params and share results
Customer to flag 8 priority prompts for manual review
Schedule infra sync to confirm VPC peering and KMS access
Follow-up meeting: 2025-03-18 10:00 PT for retest review
transcript_text:
Meeting Header: 2025-03-11 15:00 PT | Duration: 47m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (BrightHealth ML Lead), Tom Nguyen (Product), Jamal Reed (Data Eng)
---
00:00 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check 
 audio ok?
00:04 Sara: Yup, sounds good. Sorry I was on another call, thanks.
00:08 Ethan: Great. This is our weekly POC sync, main goal is to review the quality eval results from the run we did last Thursday and decide if we need prompt tuning or to rollback the quantized candidate. Maya will walk through the metrics.
00:22 Maya: cool. I shared the spreadsheet in the channel, it's the eval_20250307_quantized sheet. High-level first: overall pass rate dropped from 86% to 78% on the quantized-8bit variant. The drop concentrates in three prompt categories 
 
 insurance coverage explanation, claim denial justification, and benefit lookup multi-step prompts.
00:45 Tom: okay can you clarify what you mean by pass rate? is that the automated score or human label?
00:50 Maya: it's a combined metric 
 automatic heuristic scoring plus a small human sample to calibrate. the human pass threshold is 0.75 composite. the automatic metric tends to be optimistic, so we weight the human more.
01:05 Sara: got it. Do you have examples of failing outputs? are these hallucinations or formatting/regression style issues?
01:15 Maya: mostly factual omissions and some hallucinated policy references. for example, prompt ID A-17 
 expected to reference 'Outpatient Prior Authorization' but the response asserted a policy clause that doesn't exist. another set (B-5) truncated multi-step instruction and missed the second bullet.
01:36 Jamal: that sounds like a KV cache or past-kv issue? Could be that pruning in the quantized path is shorter?
01:44 Maya: we checked sequence length distribution, nothing dramatic. it looks like sampling/decoding interacts with quantization: temperature defaulted to 0.7 in the candidate run, when we usually use 0.2 for production.
01:58 Ethan: so two variables changed 
 quantization and decoding params. which is the likely culprit?
02:03 Maya: initial hypothesis is combined. Maya: we ran an ablation where we kept float model but used the quantized decoding path and saw a smaller drop (about 3 points), whereas quantized weights with standard decoding produced the full 8 point drop. I'm paraphrasing, the sheet has the numbers.
02:25 Sara: ok that suggests weight quantization is major factor. are there options like per-channel quantization or a higher-bit profile?
02:34 Maya: yes. Redwood supports 8-bit and 6-bit profiles and a 7-bit intermediate in internal builds 
 7-bit may reduce regressions. Also we can selectively run the high-risk prompt families on float (fallback) while keeping others on quantized 
 policy-based routing.
02:51 Tom: that hybrid approach sounds decent. what's the perf/cost delta? how much do we lose on latency/cost if we fallback to float for the top 10% prompts?
03:02 Maya: approximate: running float increases token cost ~2.5x and latency ~1.8x per request, but if it's only 10% of traffic the overall cost bump is ~20-25% and p99 latency target still attainable with headroom.
03:15 Sara: For the POC our priority is quality not minimal cost, so hybrid is acceptable if we can guarantee no regression for the top flows.
03:24 Ethan: okay practical next steps 
 Maya will produce per-prompt confusion matrices and Jamal, can you capture the exact failing payloads (inputs + metadata) so we can reproduce?
03:36 Jamal: yes I'll pull logs from our test cluster and sanitize them, send by Thursday.
03:41 Maya: also note we saw an uptick in guardrail false positives with the safety filter in the new run. Some benign medical phrasing got flagged, especially the word 'denial' used in our domain context.
03:55 Sara: that's concerning, those false positives block production. Is the safety model separate? can you tune thresholds?
04:02 Maya: Redwood's safety tier is configurable. There are two levers 
 sensitivity threshold and context-aware suppression lists. We can add a customer domain whitelist and lower sensitivity for those tokens. There's also a per-route override to bypass blocking but still log and surface alerts.
04:18 Tom: would bypassing risk compliance? we need audit trails for all bypassed responses.
04:24 Maya: yes, we keep full audit logs and redact PII. bypassed responses are logged with reason codes and timestamps; we can stream to your SIEM or put into your S3.
04:33 Sara: perfect, we need that for legal. Jamal, can you confirm KMS access for logs and whether we can maintain retention for 12 months?
04:41 Jamal: will check, our infra person is out today but I can confirm next day.
04:46 Ethan: great. Back to metrics 
 do we want Redwood to run a rerun with 7-bit or do you prefer we change decoding to lower temperature first?
04:55 Sara: let's do two parallel experiments: 1) 7-bit quant run with same decoding as prod, 2) 8-bit but forced decoding params matching prod (temp 0.2, top-p 0.95). we can compare impact.
05:09 Maya: agree. we'll queue both jobs. Expect initial results in 48 hours, full pass with human labels in 5 business days.
05:18 Tom: And for the guardrail issue?
05:21 Maya: we'll apply a domain whitelist and lower sensitivity for the flagged token list in a staging run and report false positive rate.
05:29 Sara: what's the plan for the prompt set? we've seen drift in some of our enterprise phrasing 
 should we prune or augment?
05:36 Ethan: good question. Sara: you mentioned earlier you're going to mark priority prompt sets 
 can you explain criteria?
05:41 Sara: sure. priority A = revenue-critical flows (appeal resolution, eligibility checks), B = high-frequency but lower revenue, C = exploratory. we'll send the list today.
05:50 Ethan: perfect. We'll apply the hybrid routing to A prompts first if necessary.
05:55 Maya: one more note: we observed some mismatch between the API client we used vs your production integration 
 the request showed an extra metadata field that altered context window calculation (the user_id string appended to prompt). small, but caused a few off-by-one truncations. Jamal if you can confirm client library version?
06:11 Jamal: yep we're on client v1.3.2, production uses v1.4. we'll align and retest.
06:17 Ethan: ok that could explain some truncation artifacts. Good catch.
06:21 Tom: on the question of dedicated vs hosted for the pilot 
 if we need VPC/KMS for logs and stricter SLA, will dedicated be simple to spin up?
06:32 Maya: Redwood Dedicated can be provisioned for pilots. For a short pilot we offer a burst/dedicated bridge model 
 faster, but requires a short procurement. Provisioning timeline ~2-3 weeks for dedicated with VPC peering and KMS setup; hosted mode with VPC peering (Private) is faster if you want to avoid capacity commits.
06:51 Sara: 2-3 weeks is ok if quality stabilizes. we might start hosted with VPC and then move to dedicated at contract stage.
06:59 Ethan: noted. I'll follow up on pricing options and handshake with your procurement.
07:05 Maya: to summarize technical asks 
 per-prompt confusion matrix, two reruns (7-bit and decoded-8bit), guardrail whitelist test, logs for failing payloads, confirm client lib version and retention/KMS details.
07:20 Sara: yep that's everything. do we have a time for the retest review?
07:24 Ethan: propose 2025-03-18 10:00 PT. agrees?
07:28 Sara: yes.
07:30 Ethan: great. I'll send calendar invite and the updated eval spreadsheet after we run the parallel jobs. Thanks everyone.
07:36 Tom: thanks.
07:38 Jamal: thanks all, sending logs by Thursday.
07:40 Meeting end.
